avoid: unverifiable superlatives (blazingly fast or powerful or amazing)
instead: the spec that makes the claim true (number or benchmark link or behavior)
example: avoid 'Blazingly fast build tool' - instead 'Bundles 10k modules in under 1s (benchmarks/)'

instead: the user capability those features deliver
example: avoid '20+ features for image processing' - instead 'Crop + resize + convert images from one CLI'
avoid 'Works everywhere' - instead 'Linux + macOS + Windows; Node 18+'

avoid: describing internals ('uses a hash map for O(1) lookups')
instead: the observable result for the user
example: avoid 'Uses an LRU cache internally' - instead 'Repeated queries return instantly'

instead: tense that matches reality; unbuilt items go under a Roadmap heading
example: avoid 'Supports SFTP' (planned) - instead 'SFTP support is planned (v2)'

instead: one command + one sentence per step
example: avoid a 5-line paragraph about installation - instead 'pip install name' then 'name init'

instead: plain headings; visuals only in the hero block
example: avoid '## 🚀 Quick Start ✨' - instead '## Quick start'

instead: a Limitations/Known issues section; honesty reads as reliability
example: avoid omitting 'no Windows support' - instead a '## Limitations' section stating it
